title: PHASE15-MATRIX — Calibrated Results of the Phase 1.5 Structural-Axis Scan (Indonesia)
content:
# PHASE15-MATRIX — Calibrated Results of the Phase 1.5 Structural-Axis Scan (Indonesia)

Calibration date: 2026-07-29. Protocol committed: 2026-07-29, before scoring (research/PHASE15-PROTOCOL.md). Rubric unchanged from research/RUBRIC.md (committed 2026-07-28). Inputs: 26 candidate profiles (research/axes/), raw scores from 9 independent agents, the Phase 1 matrix (research/PHASE1-MATRIX.md) for continuity, and two adversarial memos (research/verify/mining-nickel.md from Phase 1; research/verify/gold-bullion.md, the Round 1 leftover executed in this run).

## 1. Method and protocol reference

Phase 1.5 is the single logged relaxation after Phase 1's empty result: the scan widened along five structural axes while the rubric, anchors, four-part kill test, and 7.0 bar stayed fixed. Weighted score = 0.20·severity + 0.20·market + 0.15·WTP + 0.15·chain + 0.10·urgency + 0.10·competition + 0.10·moat. Any kill-test failure eliminates regardless of score. Verification triggers were widened from Phase 1: an adversarial memo is required for raw weighted ≥6.0, OR blockchain necessity ≥7, OR competition ≥7.

**Hypothesis under test (H1):** there exist trust failures in or adjacent to the Indonesian economy where (a) no single institution is accepted as anchor by every economically relevant party, AND (b) the failure supports a ≥7.0 venture built as custodian-independent verification infrastructure. Pre-registered predictions: P1 — survivors, if any, concentrate in axes 1, 2A, 2B, 3; P2 (control) — axis 5 candidates fail because a single sovereign can designate a canonical operator by decree. Falsification: an empty result across axes 1–3 means H1 is unsupported at venture scale in Indonesia.

**Calibration process.** This pass (single judge) (i) recomputed every weighted score from the raw dimension scores — all 26 match the agents' arithmetic to one decimal; (ii) applied the Phase 1 normalization rules strictly: market ≥6 on "(unverified)" sizing drops to 5, competition ≥7 without a verify memo drops, refuted gap claims cap competition at 4, scores resting on refuted premises re-anchor, collusion-tainted (COLL) sizing is stripped; (iii) re-applied the kill test to all 26; (iv) tested P1/P2 and stated the H1 verdict; (v) incorporated the gold-bullion memo into the Phase 1 record.

**Normalization outcome: zero adjustments required.** No candidate has a market score above 5 (every market 5 that rests on an unverified basis — inventory-finance, rwa-tokenization, ai-agent-authority — sits in the conservative default band the rule points to, flagged "(unverified)" in-file). No candidate has competition ≥7; the two competition-6 scores (receivables-registry, land-double-pjb) rest on searches documented inside the files per the evidence rule, are self-capped below whitespace ("MonetaGo/FCI adjacency and state absorption risk cap the openness"; "the state is visibly circling it"), and both candidates fail the kill test regardless. No blockchain-necessity score exceeds 6. Every file whose headline losses are collusion losses (12 of 26, including cross-border-receivables, inventory-finance, fund-custody-nav, timber-svlk, one-map-overlap, music-royalties) strips them from addressable sizing explicitly. The 9 agents internalized Phase 1's calibration corrections; the raw scores are the normalized scores. The consequence: the results below are not produced by judge-side adjustment — they are what the agents themselves found under the pre-committed anchors.

## 2. Ranked matrix (all 26)

Verdict key: KILL = failed kill test (all 26). EXPL = axis-4 exploratory cohort, scored but excluded from H1 statistics. No candidate passed the kill test; no candidate reached 7.0 (maximum 5.8).

| # | Candidate | Axis | Core trust failure | Norm. | Verdict | Kill reason (one line) |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | Halal mutual recognition | 1 | No global halal anchor; importers re-audit per market; BPJPH gates imports 17 Oct 2026 | 5.8 | KILL | Recognition gap is doctrinal (standards, fatwa sovereignty), not record integrity; states are shipping the fix via MRAs and BPJPH Decree 221/2025; compliance value flows to state fee schedules and accredited auditors. |
| 2 | Timber legality abroad (SVLK/FLEGT) | 1 | Foreign verifiers discount SVLK; forged V-Legal/SKSHHK documents; EUDR from 30 Dec 2026 | 5.7 | KILL | Best-evidenced failure in the cohort, but the EU regulator accepts centralized operator-side due-diligence SaaS; osapiens/Koltiva-class vendors already ingest SVLK documents and geolocation (tests 2, 3). |
| 3 | Receivables uniqueness registry | 2B | Same invoice financed at multiple lenders; SLIK borrower-keyed, FDC P2P-only | 5.6 | KILL | A central hash registry under the accepted OJK/AFPI anchor suffices — MonetaGo itself dropped DLT; thin per-check economics; realistic endgame is association/state absorption (test 2; test 4 doubtful). |
| 4 | Cross-border receivables double-financing | 1 | Same export invoice/BL financed across jurisdictions; duplicates surface at default | 5.3 | KILL | Swift/MonetaGo centralized hash registry is accepted by both sides; Indonesia coverage is an incumbent rollout, not whitespace (tests 2, 3). |
| 5 | Inventory/receivables fabrication in lending | 2B | Fabricated inventory and receivables behind bank working capital (SNP, AISA, eFishery) | 5.2 | KILL | Fungible stock cannot be made unique by any ledger — the binding oracle is physical attestation (Sucofindo/SGS) plus honest audit; collusion-stripped sizing is thin (tests 2, 4). |
| 6 | One-Map permit overlaps | 5-CTRL | Ministries issue rights from contradictory maps; 77.3M ha indicated overlap (Auriga/Kemenko 2022) | 5.1 | KILL | Sovereign is the accepted arbiter and is forcing one map by decree and task force (Perpres 5/2025; Satgas PKH: 5.8M ha seized, Rp10.27T fines by May 2026); a ledger notarizes contradictions it cannot adjudicate. |
| 7 | Pre-title property double-selling (PPJB) | 2B | Same pre-title unit sold twice via notarial PPJBs registered nowhere | 5.0 | KILL | Anchor absent, not rejected — every party accepts BPN/notariat; a state PPJB registry (one Permen amendment riding BENAR-PKP) closes it (tests 2, 3; 4 doubtful). |
| 8 | Music royalty collection (LMKN) | 3 | State collecting society's own integrity contested by beneficiaries; Rp70.44B unclaimed (LMKN, 2026) | 4.9 | KILL | Contested anchor without economics: ~US$12M national pool under an 8% opex cap funds no company, and the state is re-anchoring by decree (Permenkum 27/2025, SILM) (tests 3, 4). |
| 9 | AI agent identity & payment authority | 4-EXPL | No anchor for agent identity/mandates across platforms, merchants, rails | 4.8 | EXPL-KILL | Visa, Mastercard, Google/FIDO, Stripe and the x402 consortium shipped agent trust as features of existing rails in 2025–26; realized fee pools low-millions (tests 3, 4). |
| 10 | RWA tokenization under OJK regime | 4-EXPL | Token backing rests on issuer-custodian self-attestation | 4.8 | EXPL-KILL | OJK+KSEI are anchors every party accepts; the state itself ships the regime (RWA POJK targeted Q3-2026); sandbox winners are custodian businesses, not custodian-independent verification (tests 2, 3). |
| 11 | AI training-data licensing provenance | 4-EXPL | Labs scrape Indonesian content; no anchor accepted by labs and publishers | 4.8 | EXPL-KILL | Cloudflare/TollBit occupy the crawl-consent chokepoint as tolerated single operators; training-set proof is unsolvable by any registry; Indonesia flow single-digit $M/yr (unverified) (tests 2-weak, 3, 4). |
| 12 | Digital ad spend reconciliation | 3 | Platform self-reporting; Indonesian IVT 59.17% (Fraudlogix, Q1 2026) | 4.6 | KILL | MRC-accredited verifiers are the accepted anchor where data access exists; walled gardens refuse to feed any ledger, so custodian-independent proof cannot bootstrap (tests 2, 3). |
| 13 | Seafarer certificate verification (foreign) | 1 | Forgery syndicate compromised the state registry itself (5,041 fakes, 2018–2020) | 4.4 | KILL | STCW treaty makes the issuing state the accepted anchor; Kemenhub's free portal and QR e-certs ship the fix; no verified third-party spend (tests 2, 3, 4). |
| 14 | Fund NAV & custody attestation | 2A | Post-Jiwasraya/Asabri NAV manipulation via insider-controlled underlyings | 4.3 | KILL | KSEI S-INVEST is the accepted single-operator ledger; losses were off-system collusion a ledger records immutably but does not stop; oversight is FundGuard-class SaaS (tests 2, 3; 4 doubtful). |
| 15 | Crypto proof of reserves | 2A | Voluntary PoR atop OJK's licensed exchange-clearing-custody structure | 4.3 | KILL | OJK/CFX/KKI anchor accepted by all parties; exchanges self-publish PoR and OJK can mandate by SEOJK; ~27 institutional buyers (tests 2, 3, 4). |
| 16 | Foreign KYC on Indonesian corporates | 1 | Language/rails friction, self-declared BO data, notary-forged deeds | 4.3 | KILL | Foreign verifiers accept the state anchor (AHU extract + QR e-apostille under the Hague Convention); contested cases were resolved by treating AHU as authoritative; aggregators serve the friction (tests 2, 3). |
| 17 | Electronic bills of lading (MLETR) | 1 | Paper B/L originals; eBLs lack document-of-title force under Indonesian law | 4.0 | KILL | Ten IGP&I-approved platforms are accepted anchors on both sides; DCSA interop live June 2026; the gap is statutory, fixable only by the state (tests 2, 3, 4). |
| 18 | Fidusia double-pledging | 2B | Same movable asset pledged to multiple lenders; AHU registry never enforced uniqueness | 4.0 | KILL | Accepted anchors consolidating by decree — AHU 2024 double-registration restriction, OJK-mandated Rapindo (POJK 47/2020), e-BPKB 2027; gap is compliance, not contested trust (tests 2, 3, 4). |
| 19 | Article 6 carbon transfers | 1 | Corresponding adjustments slow; only one completed 6.2 transfer by Apr 2025 | 3.9 | KILL | Both sovereigns accept UNFCCC CARP and the JCM Joint Committee as anchors; the state builds blockchain SRUK itself; cumulative traded value ~US$3–5M (tests 2, 3, 4). |
| 20 | Health-worker credential mobility | 1 | Every destination re-verifies Indonesian nurse credentials from scratch | 3.9 | KILL | Accepted intermediaries exist per corridor (DataFlow, GIZ, JICWELS); outflows in low thousands/yr put verification spend at single-digit $M (tests 2, 3, 4). |
| 21 | Client fund segregation attestation | 2A | Broker/PSP client-fund misuse (Sarijaya-era pooled cash) | 3.9 | KILL | The state already shipped the independent second ledger by decree after Sarijaya (KSEI AKSes, client-name RDN, BI float rules); accepted by every party (tests 2, 3, 4). |
| 22 | Digital gold custody attestation | 2A | Does physical gold back app-sold digital gold? | 3.8 | KILL | 1:1 depository plus clearing under Bappebti/OJK accepted by all parties; regime already shipped; <10 platforms plus 2 bullion banks as buyers (tests 2, 3, 4). |
| 23 | Coalition loyalty point liabilities | 3 | Bilateral batch settlement; breakage on one ledger | 3.8 | KILL | The coalition operator's ledger is the contractually accepted anchor; SaaS incumbents ship settlement; coalition slice of US$1.03B loyalty spend (ResearchAndMarkets, 2025) far under $50M (tests 2, 3, 4). |
| 24 | Multi-agency fisheries export clearance | 5-CTRL | Document relay across KKP, BPPMHKP, Barantin, Customs | 3.7 | KILL | INSW is the mandated integrator accepted by all parties and consolidating now (SSm QC; SMKHP–KI-1 pilot July 2026; IBOSS); EU/US/Japan accept flag-state certificates by treaty (tests 2, 3, 4). |
| 25 | Warehouse receipt integrity (SRG) | 2A | Receipt forgery/double-pledge risk in resi gudang | 3.0 | KILL | Statutory KBI registry (blockchain-based IS-Ware since 2020) accepted by banks and Bappebti; no in-registry fraud documented; ~Rp2T system too small (tests 2, 3, 4). |
| 26 | Inter-ministry carbon accounting | 5-CTRL | One ton of CO2e in four state ledgers | 2.5 | KILL | Control confirmed: the sovereign decreed a canonical owner — SRN PPI Terintegrasi ships July 2026 as the single national platform; ~US$3.2M exchange turnover (tests 2, 3, 4). |

## 3. Kill-test survivors

**None.** All 26 candidates fail at least one kill test in their own agents' files, and this calibration confirms every failure against the file evidence. There is consequently no survivor paragraph to write: the nearest miss, halal-mutual-recognition (5.8), fails because tamper-evidence changes no importing regulator's behavior — a cryptographically immutable BPJPH certificate is still rejected if the slaughter method fails the destination's fatwa — and the fix is shipping by treaty (52 MRAs; BPJPH Decree 221/2025). Timber-svlk (5.7) is the best-evidenced trust failure of the cohort (SKSHHK serial reuse seizure, Balikpapan, 6 July 2026; EIA 2021 certified-illegal-timber findings) and still fails because the EU competent authority accepts centralized operator-side due-diligence platforms the incumbents already sell. Receivables-registry (5.6) fails because the accepted-anchor version of itself — a centralized hash registry under OJK/AFPI — is strictly simpler, as MonetaGo's own abandonment of blockchain demonstrates (GTR, 2022).

## 4. H1 / P1 / P2 verdicts

**H1: UNSUPPORTED at venture scale in Indonesia.** The falsification condition fires: the result across axes 1–3 (20 candidates, axis 4 excluded) is empty — zero kill-test survivors, zero candidates at ≥7.0, maximum normalized score 5.8, and no candidate even reached the widened adversarial-memo triggers (max raw weighted 5.8 < 6.0; max chain 6 < 7; max competition 6 < 7). The two H1 conjuncts fail in a specific, informative pattern:

- Where conjunct (a) genuinely holds — no universally accepted anchor — conjunct (b) fails. The cohort contains five real anchor-less or contested-anchor failures: halal recognition (doctrinal sovereignty), timber acceptance (foreign discounting of SVLK), ad reconciliation (walled gardens reject every anchor), music royalties (the custodian's integrity itself contested on the street, June 2026), and AI data licensing (labs and publishers accept no common anchor). Every one dies on economics or on the discovery that tamper-evidence does not change the controlling party's behavior. Two agent-stated refinements deserve carrying forward: ad-reconciliation shows a "custodian refuses all anchors" case is as fatal as an accepted anchor, because custodian-independent proof cannot bootstrap without the custodian's data; music-royalties shows a contested anchor is necessary but not sufficient — the disputed pool must also be large enough to fund independent verification.
- Where the economics are real (receivables, inventory finance, cross-border trade finance), conjunct (a) fails: adversarial lenders still accept state/association anchors, and the strongest evidence is that the category leader (MonetaGo) removed blockchain from its own product.

**P1 (survivors concentrate in axes 1/2A/2B/3): vacuously satisfied, not confirmed.** There are no survivors anywhere, so the prediction's antecedent is unmet. Directionally, the top five scores are all axis 1/2B (5.8, 5.7, 5.6, 5.3, 5.2), but an axis-5 control (one-map, 5.1) outscored 15 of the 20 axis 1–3 candidates, so weighted-score concentration is weak evidence at best. P1 carries no confirmatory weight in this run.

**P2 (axis-5 controls fail): CONFIRMED, 3 of 3, by the predicted mechanism.** Every control was killed specifically because a single sovereign designated (or is designating) a canonical operator by decree: SRN PPI Terintegrasi as the single national climate platform (July 2026); Perpres 5/2025 plus Satgas PKH enforcement for one-map; INSW/PP 25/2025 consolidation with the SMKHP–KI-1 integration pilot (22 July 2026) for fisheries. Carbon-interministry produced the lowest score in the cohort (2.5) — exactly what a working control should do. The control results validate that the kill test discriminates rather than failing everything indiscriminately for trivial reasons: score dispersion across the cohort runs 2.5–5.8, and the controls fail by the specific predicted mechanism (sovereign decree), not by the generic ones.

**Consequence per protocol:** the project reverts to the Phase 1 option-B shapes or stop-and-monitor. Phase 2 deep-dive budget should not be spent disproving what two phases now show independently.

## 5. Exploratory cohort report (Axis 4 — excluded from H1 statistics)

The three new-market candidates scored 4.8 each and all failed the kill test — but the question they answer is different: whether newly forming markets emerge decentralized. The finding is one consistent negative: **the trust layer of each new market was captured by incumbents or consortia before a neutral startup position could form.** Agent identity and payment mandates shipped as features of existing rails (Visa Trusted Agent Protocol, Mastercard Agent Pay, Google AP2/FIDO, OpenAI–Stripe ACP, x402 under the Linux Foundation) within roughly a year of the problem being articulated. RWA tokenization in Indonesia formed inside the OJK sandbox from day one — the licensed positions are custodian businesses, with the state shipping the regime itself (RWA POJK targeted Q3-2026). AI data licensing's verifiable surface (crawl/consent) was occupied by Cloudflare/TollBit, while the genuinely unsolved part — proving a work entered a completed model's training set — is unsolvable by any registry, decentralized or not. Exploratory conclusion: new-market emergence in 2025–26 ran *toward* incumbent-anchored trust, not away from it; the axis-4 cohort offers no refuge from the H1 result and no case for re-running Phase 1.5 on future new markets absent a structural change (e.g., a regulator mandating custodian-independent proof).

## 6. Shortlist (unpadded)

**Empty.** No candidate passed the kill test; no candidate reached 7.0 normalized (maximum 5.8). Per the pre-registered protocol and the standing instruction, the shortlist is not padded. This is the second consecutive empty result under the same rubric, produced this time by nine independent agents whose raw scores required zero calibration adjustments — the result is not an artifact of judge-side normalization.

## 7. Gold-bullion verdict update (Phase 1 continuity)

The Round 1 leftover memo (research/verify/gold-bullion.md, executed 2026-07-29) **REFUTES** the Phase 1 whitespace claim, and the Phase 1 gold verdict is updated from SCORE (5.9, sole kill-test survivor) to **REFUTED/KILL**:

- The literal claim ("no Indonesian startup does custodian-independent gold provenance/PoR") remains true, but the commercial whitespace it implied has closed: Blocktogo (PT Indonesia Blockchain Persada) graduated OJK's IAKD sandbox 8 Aug 2025 with GIDR gold tokenization custodied at Pegadaian — the anchor custodian partnered, and not with a verification startup; the FAQ discloses no third-party audit or PoR mechanism (goidr.co.id).
- Phase 1's kill condition (a) materially advanced: LBMA reports 100% of Good Delivery refiners on the GBI database (aXedras) as of start-2026, with Antam exonerated by the LBMA Incident Review and inside the perimeter.
- Phase 1's kill condition (b) is the regulatory trajectory: the OJK Bullion Roadmap 2026–2031 (launched 6–7 Mar 2026), POJK 2/2026 (gold ETF), and PADK 3/2026 all point to centralized regulator-facing reporting. The named revival trigger — a custodian-independent PoR mandate — did not fire; no such rulemaking exists in any 2025–26 OJK or Bappebti instrument found.
- Consequences applied per rubric: the refuted gap claim caps competition at 4 (it already stood at 4; the memo judges even that generous); kill tests 2, 3, and 4 now fail (state-anchored trust stack accepted by every monetizable buyer; incumbents/state shipping; buyer universe absorbed into the stack). **Phase 1's kill-test-survivor count falls from one to zero**, strengthening the Phase 1 empty result retroactively.
- Surviving fragment (not the scored venture): retail secondary-market bar authentication independent of Antam (fake CertiCards, pawn/marketplace flows) plus third-party reserve attestation for OJK-sandbox gold-token issuers — an assay/audit-service niche.

Consistency check against Phase 1.5: the digital-gold-custody candidate (axis 2A, 3.8, KILL) was scored on premises the memo confirms rather than contradicts — its incumbent list already included Kinesis and the Bappebti depository chain, and its kill reasoning matches the memo's finding that the state absorbed the trust layer. No Phase 1.5 score rested on the refuted premise; no re-anchoring was required.

## 8. Verification log

- **Memos triggered in Phase 1.5: 0 of 26.** Under the widened pre-registered triggers (raw weighted ≥6.0, chain ≥7, or competition ≥7), no candidate qualified: maxima were 5.8 weighted (halal-mutual-recognition), 6 chain (timber-svlk, halal, music-royalties, ai-agent-authority, ai-data-licensing), 6 competition (receivables-registry, land-double-pjb). The absence of triggers is itself information: scores sat far enough below the bar that no whitespace claim required adversarial testing.
- **Memos executed: 1** — gold-bullion (Round 1 leftover, 2026-07-29): REFUTED (§7). Disclosed limitation: its web search degraded mid-run to Google News RSS and direct fetches; the "no new private competitor" finding is weaker than the buyer-path-closing finding, which rests on primary/state sources (OJK, LBMA, Bappebti).
- **Calibration adjustments: none** (§1). Arithmetic re-verified for all 26; anchor-consistency checked dimension-by-dimension against each file's stated justifications; the two competition-6 scores verified against in-file documented searches; COLL stripping verified present in every file whose headline losses are collusion losses.
- **Kill-test re-application: 26 of 26 fail**, confirmed against file evidence (kill sections quoted in each profile). Modal failure: test 2 (an accepted trusted operator exists or suffices), consistent with Phase 1's central finding.
- **Evidence-rule enforcement:** all sizing figures in this matrix carry their in-file citations or "(unverified)"; extrapolations flagged in files (ad-waste nine-figure estimate, agent-fee pools, RWA fee-pool derivation, Indonesia licensing flows) remain unverified here and were scored in the conservative bands.
- **Standing caveats carried forward from Phase 1:** several secondary sources repeating one figure count as one source; "nobody built this" claims without a memo remain unproven (none at consequence-bearing thresholds this round); off-system collusion losses remain outside any verification product's reach.
